old:
Within each run, the estimates average diagnostic records with replay
measurements and an available fresh-response length, using the most recent
length measurement if it is not in the same record. Run estimates then receive
equal weight within each model--domain cell. Repeated step records are not
deduplicated, and records are not truncated to the 3,072-update horizon. Fresh-group token
counts are reconstructed from logged response lengths and a prompt-length
estimate derived from replay rows. These are descriptive workload summaries,
not a cumulative compute audit. They exclude rollout generation, padding,
attention-specific costs, activation recomputation, verification, bank
maintenance, optimizer work, communication, and evaluation. Hardware pools
also differ across cohorts. Neither these estimates nor the reference-KL
comparison establishes an end-to-end speedup or resolves the missing budget
control.
new:
Workload estimates are averaged within runs and then equally across seeds
in each model--domain cell. Fresh-group token counts use response lengths
and prompt-length estimates. These averages describe the selected likelihood
passes, not cumulative computation through the matched training horizon.
They exclude rollout generation, padding, attention-specific costs,
activation recomputation, verification, bank maintenance, optimizer work,
communication, and evaluation. They therefore do not establish an
end-to-end speedup or an advantage at equal total compute.
reason: Keep workload averaging/estimand/exclusions; move log-join/duplicate/truncation implementation to code.
